headline.headline: MARLINS STORM BACK FROM FOUR DOWN TO SINK PHILLIES, 8-6
headline.deck: Miami erupts for six unanswered runs across the seventh and eighth innings at loanDepot park
headline.body:
MIAMI — The Philadelphia Phillies led by four runs heading into the bottom of the seventh inning Wednesday night and looked every bit like a club about to take control of the series. Instead, the Miami Marlins turned loanDepot park into bedlam, plating three runs in the seventh and two more in the eighth to stun the Phillies, 8-6, before 14,350 fans.

Philadelphia had built its advantage methodically — two runs in the third, one in the fourth, and three more in a pivotal fifth inning that had the visitors feeling comfortable. Miami answered with three of its own in the fifth to stay within striking distance, then held the Phillies scoreless over the final four frames. The seventh-inning uprising broke the game open, and the Marlins tacked on two insurance runs in the eighth, one of them on a home run by a pinch hitter who had entered for Navarreto — Navarreto himself having been hit by a Jesus Luzardo pitch earlier in the contest. Trea Turner homered for Philadelphia, but it was not enough.

Sidney Johnson earned the win on the mound for Miami in a game completed in two hours and 29 minutes. The Phillies, unable to protect a four-run cushion, depart South Florida with the kind of loss that lingers in a clubhouse for days.

secondary.headline: LAUER DEALS AS DODGERS CLIP MARINERS, 4-2
secondary.deck: Left-hander Eric Lauer throws one-hit ball over six innings; Andy Pages goes deep for Los Angeles
secondary.body:
LOS ANGELES — Eric Lauer was untouchable for six innings Wednesday, holding the Seattle Mariners to a single hit and no runs as the Los Angeles Dodgers rolled to a 4-2 victory. Lauer's outing was the kind of vintage starting-pitcher performance that Dodgers fans have come to expect from a rotation stacked with options.

Andy Pages provided the offensive punch that mattered most, launching a home run to stake Los Angeles to a lead it would not relinquish. The Dodgers bullpen held on despite a late Seattle push, and the win kept Los Angeles rolling through the heart of the summer schedule.

secondary.headline: MCKENNA ARRIVES: TOP DRAFT PICK SETS HIS SIGHTS ON NHL STAGE
secondary.deck: Gavin McKenna, first overall pick in 2026, outlines rookie season goals at NHLPA Showcase
secondary.body:
The 2026 NHL Draft's top pick, Gavin McKenna, stepped before cameras Wednesday at the NHLPA Rookie Showcase and spoke plainly about what he intends to accomplish in his first professional season. McKenna, whose selection generated the kind of anticipation that surrounds generational prospects, said he is focused on earning ice time and contributing immediately rather than easing into the league.

McKenna's arrival comes as the NHL playoffs grind through the second round, offering the teenager a front-row education in what postseason hockey demands. Whether the franchise that drafted him is still alive in May will shape the environment he walks into, but by all accounts McKenna's preparation and maturity suggest he will not need long to make his presence felt.

secondary.headline: GARRETT THROWS OPEN THE DOOR FOR DONALD'S RETURN
secondary.deck: Rams defensive tackle Myles Garrett says he would welcome a partnership with retired legend Aaron Donald
secondary.body:
Myles Garrett, who joined the Los Angeles Rams this offseason and has quickly become the centerpiece of their defensive line plans, made clear Wednesday that he would have no objection to sharing that line with Aaron Donald if the retired three-time Defensive Player of the Year chose to end his retirement. Garrett called the possibility exciting and said the football world would benefit from seeing Donald back on the field.

Donald, who retired after the 2023 season, has not made any formal indication that a return is imminent, but Garrett's public enthusiasm adds fuel to speculation that has simmered through training camp. The Rams, who open a new chapter under their current roster construction, would present Donald with a ready-made contending defense should he decide the itch to play is too strong to ignore.

column.headline: MIAMI'S COMEBACK IS A WARNING SHOT FOR A PHILLIES TEAM THAT CANNOT HOLD LEADS
column.body:
There is no comfortable lead against a desperate baseball team in July, and the Philadelphia Phillies learned that lesson the hard way Wednesday night in Miami. Leading by four runs with six outs to go and watching a Marlins club that drew fewer than 15,000 fans to the ballpark, the Phillies did not simply lose a game. They surrendered five runs without reply in a span of two innings and walked out of loanDepot park looking like a team that does not trust itself when it matters.

The Phillies have too much talent to keep dropping games this way, and Trea Turner's home run is cold comfort when the bullpen cannot protect a four-run cushion in late July. Miami is not supposed to be this team's problem. If the Phillies cannot figure out how to slam the door on a rebuilding club playing in front of a modest crowd on a Wednesday night, the questions about this roster will only get louder as October approaches.

story.headline: ORIOLES RALLY FROM SEVEN DOWN, EDGE TIGERS IN 12 TO COMPLETE WILD COMEBACK
story.deck: Baltimore wipes out a 7-0 deficit, winning in extra innings on a walk-off single
story.body:
DETROIT — The Baltimore Orioles spotted the Detroit Tigers seven runs, watched starter after starter falter across six innings, and then proceeded to do the unthinkable at Comerica Park on Wednesday night, staging a furious comeback that stretched into the 12th inning before Baltimore finally walked away with a 10-9 victory before 34,406 stunned fans.

The Tigers built their lead in chunks — three runs in the third, two more in the fifth, and two in the sixth — and appeared to be coasting toward a comfortable win. Then the seventh inning arrived. The Orioles erupted for five runs in that frame alone, cutting the deficit to two, and added two more in the eighth to pull even at nine. Zach Vierling tripled and doubled for Detroit in a losing effort, while Colt Keith also tripled and Matt Torkelson slugged his 20th home run of the season. Baltimore's Jackson Holliday swiped a base during the rally, and Coby Mayo laced a triple as part of the surge. The two clubs left a combined 45 runners on base across 12 exhausting innings.

With the score knotted at nine heading to the 12th, Baltimore pushed across the decisive run to seal the comeback and hand Detroit a gut-punch defeat. The game consumed three hours and 33 minutes, the longest of Wednesday's slate, and stood as the most dramatic result of the day in a packed schedule that also saw the San Francisco Giants pummel Milwaukee 16-3, highlighted by a seven-run sixth inning, and the Miami Marlins rally past Philadelphia 8-6 on the strength of home runs from Trea Turner, Enrique Hernandez, and Griffin Conine.

story.headline: CLIPPERS SALARY CAP PROBE COULD STRETCH INTO 2027 AS LEONARD QUESTIONS LOOM OVER FRANCHISE
story.deck: The NBA's investigation into Los Angeles may reshape the league's financial landscape for years.
story.body:
The NBA's investigation into the Los Angeles Clippers and superstar forward Kawhi Leonard shows no signs of reaching a swift resolution, with league sources indicating the probe could extend well into 2027. At the heart of the inquiry are allegations that the Clippers circumvented salary cap regulations to compensate Leonard in ways that violated collective bargaining rules, a charge that carries potentially severe consequences ranging from draft pick forfeiture to heavy financial penalties. The franchise, already navigating uncertainty around Leonard's health and future, now faces an institutional cloud that threatens to define its near-term trajectory.

The investigation adds another layer of turbulence to a league already buzzing with seismic player movement. LeBron James, the 22-time All-Star, confirmed his decision to sign with the Philadelphia 76ers in what sources close to the situation describe as a move driven by personal loyalty and legacy rather than championship calculus. ESPN's Brian Windhorst reported on his podcast The Hoop Collective that James weighed his options carefully before choosing Philadelphia, a franchise desperate for a galvanizing force after years of injury-plagued disappointment.

Meanwhile, the debate over LeBron's legacy continued to rage off the court after former NBA champion Kendrick Perkins unloaded on Draymond Green, calling Green's recent take diminishing LeBron's accomplishments flat-out delusional. Perkins, never one to mince words, argued that Green's criticism of James reflects a fundamental misreading of what the four-time champion has meant to the modern game. With James now in Philadelphia and the Clippers mired in legal uncertainty, the 2026 offseason has delivered more drama than most playoff runs.

story.headline: CELEBRINI BECOMES HIGHEST-PAID PLAYER IN NHL HISTORY WITH MASSIVE SHARKS EXTENSION
story.deck: San Jose locks up its franchise center on a five-year, $94 million deal.
story.body:
San Jose, Calif. -- The San Jose Sharks made history Wednesday, signing second-year center Macklin Celebrini to a five-year, $94 million contract extension that carries an average annual value of $18.8 million, making the former No. 1 overall pick the highest-paid player in the history of the National Hockey League. The deal, announced by the club Wednesday afternoon, signals the organization's full commitment to building its next championship contender around the 19-year-old phenom who dazzled Sharks fans throughout his rookie campaign.

Celebrini, who was selected first overall in the 2024 NHL Draft, recorded 67 points in his debut season and earned widespread recognition as one of the most complete young centers the league has seen in years. The extension kicks in for the 2026-27 season, locking Celebrini into teal through the 2031-32 campaign. Sharks general manager Mike Grier called the signing a cornerstone moment for the franchise, which has spent recent seasons stockpiling draft capital and developing young talent after a prolonged rebuild.

The blockbuster deal arrived on the same day that No. 1 overall pick of the 2026 draft, Gavin McKenna, spoke at the NHLPA Rookie Showcase in Toronto and outlined his own ambitions for his debut season. McKenna, selected by a franchise eager to replicate exactly the kind of success San Jose is now celebrating with Celebrini, said his personal goals center on competing for the Calder Trophy and contributing to wins immediately. The two signings, taken together, painted a vivid picture of an NHL landscape shaped by generational young talent commanding generational money.

story.headline: QUARTERBACKS ON THE MOVE AS NFL OFFSEASON RESHAPES LEAGUE LANDSCAPE
story.deck: Big-name signal-callers find new homes as rosters transform ahead of training camp.
story.body:
The NFL offseason has erupted into one of the most frenetic reshuffling periods in recent memory, with quarterbacks leading the charge as franchises retool following Super Bowl LX. The Las Vegas Raiders completed a blockbuster trade last week to acquire Geno Smith from the Seattle Seahawks, sending a first-round pick and a young receiver to the Pacific Northwest in exchange for the veteran passer. Las Vegas general manager Tom Telesco called Smith the missing piece for a rebuilding squad that finished 7-10 in the 2025 season.

Meanwhile, the Carolina Panthers made waves in free agency by signing backup quarterback Bailey Zappe to a two-year deal worth $28 million, signaling the organization's intent to stabilize a position that cycled through three starters last season. The Panthers also added veteran offensive lineman Cam Robinson, released by the Jacksonville Jaguars in March, to anchor a rebuilt front five. Carolina head coach Dave Canales insisted the moves reflect a commitment to protecting whoever lines up under center in 2026.

On the draft front, analysts continue to debate the long-term value of the top picks from the 2026 NFL Draft held last month in Green Bay. Ohio State quarterback Dylan Raiola, selected third overall by the New Orleans Saints, has already reported for voluntary workouts and impressed the coaching staff with his command of the playbook. Saints offensive coordinator Klint Kubiak said Raiola's football IQ stands out among the rookie class, raising expectations that the young passer could compete for the starting role well ahead of schedule when training camp opens in late July.
